task.description:
WF-03 Step 5 -- close ISS-0200. You produced this run's diagnosis at Step 1; the closing REVIEWER gate PASSED both your NO-CHANGE verdict and the edit recording it, after one rework. Read handoffs/WF03-ISS0200-20260821/step-03c-reviewer-regate.json before starting -- it PASSES the run and then names three MINORs, two of which it says must be acted on BEFORE this step writes anything. They are not restated here.

ISS-0200 BECOMES THE FIRST RECORD IN THIS PROJECT EVER TO CARRY `status: no_defect`. Everything you write is the precedent every later no-defect record copies. A first use that does not meet its own new bar would be the worst possible precedent for it -- DOC-UPDATER flagged exactly this at Step 3 and it is the main risk of this step.

(1) WRITE docs/issues/ISS-0200.yaml TO THE BAR ITSELF. The four-item evidence bar is in docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md's "Issue status vocabulary" -- read it there and satisfy it item by item, in the record. Bar item 1 forbids inherited figures BY NAME, so the figures in the record must be the ones you measured, not the ones ISS-0200's own filing asserted; where your measurement and the filing differ, the record says so (your Step 1 result corrected the 2.1x generalisation UPWARD to 2.92x pooled -- that correction belongs in the record, not just in a handoff). Cite handoffs/WF03-ISS0200-20260821/step-005-01-diagnose.json by path for the full working. Item 2 wants the candidate mechanisms named individually INCLUDING the ones the data did not support -- that list is the part an uninvestigated issue could never fabricate, which is why the bar demands it. Item 3 wants the method's stated limitations: your own shingle-calibration caveat, and the re-gate's finding that the least-dense-file identity is metric-dependent. Do not soften either; a negative result that hides the weakness of the test that produced it is worth less than no record at all.

(2) THREE ONE-LINE DOC CORRECTIONS THE RE-GATE NAMED. ORCH rules all three in scope for this step -- two because the gate says they must land before this record is written, the third because it is a factual inaccuracy this run introduced into a canonical document and it is two words.

  (a) KEY-NAME COLLISION. ORCH RULES: rename the pair to `verdict_in_run:` / `verdict_at:` in ISSUE_QUEUE.md, rather than the gate's other option of keeping `closed_*` at top level with a stated meaning. Reasons, so you can overturn this if you find it wrong rather than merely comply: `closed_at` already means "when GitHub closed the issue" at ISS-0109.yaml:314, and a registry ISS-0191's linter is meant to read mechanically should not carry one key with two meanings distinguished only by nesting depth; `verdict_*` is self-describing and cannot collide with a GitHub close at any nesting level; and no record uses it yet, so the rename costs one line now and a sweep later. If you disagree, say so in result.issues and state what you did -- HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 1.1 governs, and a verified disagreement outranks this dispatch. Whichever pair you land on, ISS-0200 must then USE it, and the record should make plain what the timestamp measures.

  (b) WF-03 STEP 5's OWN PSEUDOCODE. Two parts in docs/agents/workflows/WF-03_issue_resolving.md, both in the block you are executing right now, which is why they are yours. Item 1's template still opens with a concrete copyable `status: resolved` line; make the template name the alternatives so a weak model copying line one cannot land on the wrong status. Item 2 hardcodes a GitHub close comment reading "Fixed in <run-id>... and the regression test at <path>" -- on a no-defect close that publishes a false resolution claim to an external audience and cites a regression test this run does not have. Make item 2 branch on the status.

  (c) THE ISS-0202 GLOSS. HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's new parenthetical glosses ISS-0202 as measuring handoffs whose artifacts_out names ONLY their own file; ISS-0202 measured the broader "lists their own handoff file as one of their outputs". Correct the gloss to match what ISS-0202 actually says. Do not add a figure -- the re-gate specifically confirmed no number is smuggled back in under the citation, and that must stay true.

(3) CLOSE THE GITHUB ISSUE, #391, per WF-03 Step 5 item 2 -- but write the comment yourself under (2)(b)'s corrected form. It must not claim a fix, must not cite a regression test, and must state plainly that the issue was investigated and measured to carry no defect, pointing at docs/issues/ISS-0200.yaml and the diagnosis handoff. This comment is the one artefact an outside reader sees without following a pointer, so it carries the same honesty burden the record does.

DO NOT: reopen the NO-CHANGE verdict or anything else this run's gates certified; touch HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 4 or section 2's four worked examples (ISS-0200 AC4 protects them and they have now been certified byte-identical twice); re-edit ISS-0191.yaml or the H-SIZE-3 Enforcement extension; or absorb the sha-recording finding, which is filed as ISS-0205.

Re-verify AC4 byte-identity after your edits and quote it, exactly as Step 3 did -- you are touching the same file and this is the third time that span has needed protecting. Commit by explicit filename. ORCH runs a short closing gate on this step before Step Final, so state your evidence in a form a validator can re-derive.
acceptance_criteria: docs/issues/ISS-0200.yaml carries the new terminal status and satisfies all four items of ISSUE_QUEUE.md's evidence bar IN THE RECORD, item by item, with figures you measured rather than inherited from the filing, citing the diagnosis handoff by path
The record states the correction to ISS-0200's own 2.1x generalisation (2.92x pooled) rather than leaving it only in a handoff

The record names the candidate mechanisms individually including those the data did not support, and states the method limitations unsoftened -- both the shingle calibration caveat and the metric-dependence of the least-dense-file identity
The key pair is settled and used consistently: ORCH's ruling applied, or overturned with the disagreement and reasoning stated in result.issues per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL section 1.1
WF-03 Step 5's item-1 template no longer leads with a concrete wrong status, and item 2's GitHub close comment branches on the status
The ISS-0202 gloss in HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md matches what ISS-0202 actually measured, with no figure added
GH#391 closed with a comment that claims no fix, cites no regression test, and states the no-defect outcome plainly (quote the comment and the gh command output)
ISS-0200 AC4 re-verified post-edit and quoted: section 4 and section 2's four worked examples still byte-identical to merge-base 7322185
Edits committed by explicit filename; git status --porcelain quoted at completion
